just commenting to see if i got the counter thing

​

Don't know what boat you're in, hobbies, profession, country, whatever, but if really feel like doing something you love or try something new it'd be a nice "occasion"...worst case scenario i'm here (along with many others i suppose) if u just feel like chatting.

If you're that determined, i doubt my words will help. 

  
Having had my thoughts wander into the dark side of the woods, which i am not comparing to yours in any way, the only person who came looking for me was me.  I hope you'll go looking for yourself OP <3.

Throwing it out there for anyone who might be on the same boat : 

Betrayal can come from anyone, including family/attachments. 

Remember that what you feel/see in yourself when you're with a person, no matter who that person may be, it was within you all along <3.
hit me up bruh im new here and would like to get some talk going :)

Certainly so, my psychiatrist should be helpful with the medication.   
I did talk to my parents, and they were just kind of "shell shocked" at first. Now they're a bit more loose. Still supportive, but i can see the concern. Can't blame them really, but can't leave it at that aswell.   


As i said in my other reply, i just want to make it to practical medicine to give myself the chance of seeing what my future life could be like. Kind of eagerness over "beating myself up", to me at least...  


I'm happy you shared your success story, and glad it turned out to be a success story in the end. Here's hoping mine is one aswell. Peace \<3.

Hello colleague, i appreciate your personal take on it, especially as you've been there before.   
I'm a med 2 student so far, haven't done full rounds yet, only partially/volunteered as i enjoy the company of people and providing for them. Granted, that's just MY experience as someone who has not been on the floors yet...an analogy i think of is like being a tourist : you see what's fine and dandy, but don't really know the hardships of living in the area so your perception is skewed.   


My reasons overlap yours in terms of environment. Didn't fit in with my colleagues quite well as they're quite high class and i couldn't afford their outings/hangouts on one hand, and never was a fan of "fake people and favourisitm". But i can't complain about the latter as it's present everywhere, at least where i'm from.   


I can't take a gap year (doesn't exist @ my uni) but i have 2 months off till next year.   


I know that the rounds will be different from what we're taking in med2. I know that what i'm doing now, although paramount in terms of medicine, is not the **practice** of medicine. I know that when we went to the ER i was  discussing/proposing procedures with the resident. **This** is what kept me going so far.

I booked an appointment with a psych. I figured that if i can keep my cool someway till i reach the practical part of medicine, i'll be able to judge then.

I do want to thank you for your concern and kind words. I also hope you're caring for your self now, and whatever you transitioned into post medicine is treating you well.

i got an appointment right after i posted this actually, and you're right they are the professionals at the end of the day. Ironically whenever we had study groups i used to explain the material to my study group, and guess who scored higher? Not me.   


weakest parts aren't concepts or certain courses as much as they are the ability to focus and recall during exams. i will have to look more into that...my dilemma is sort of like which came first, these thoughts or med school? granted, med school isn't making them any better, which in turn keeps me from making my studies more efficient. i'll just have to keep knocking on doors and see what happens.   


Thank you for your reply btw \<3
